A pure-base closed halfspace through Y includes at least half the total and the entire central fiber. Tightening a containing cap preserves Y and only decreases mass.

The three canonical margins sum to zero and their caps cover the ambient space, proving the global upper bound. At any mark with nonzero continuous coordinate at least one margin is strictly positive, so its parallel cap removes a positive-area strip in the central fiber.

For each nonzero base p with continuous mark zero, an exact rational test found a positive t keeping all 25 isolated-vertex cuts in range and reducing mass. In general the tilt polynomial has strictly negative linear coefficient −(4|T|/9)109||p||² by Σr z=0, and the quadratic term is finite.

For that normal, vertex projections are (-1,-1,2), and the isolated vertex area yields paired sum (8+2s²)/9 on |s|≤1. At larger absolute shift one term is one. Thus every opposite pair forces a·z=0, and the sites span the base.

The two axis sections are [-r,r] segments and the diagonal section has length 2√2 r, all centered. Their coareas are 2r and their ambient centroid vanishes by base reflection. The minimal positive circuit is v1+v2+v3=0. Unit-normal coefficients are proportional to ||v_j||, as are their total threshold derivatives, yielding normalized response weights 1/3.

On an edge the nonactive third margin is -r, and the other two margins cross zero at 1/3 and 2/3. Source densities 3/4 and 3/2 follow. The middle branch preserves its mean, retains density one there, and transfers density 1/4 to each outer third. Edges are affine and vertices have null length, so the summed kernel preserves base, edge normal and conditional physical mean, and conditional Jensen gives the stated field inequality.

No affine upper roof support can touch both strict sides because the roof is strictly above the chord at the crease. The four indicated strict-negative sites have the four parities, and their negatives have the same parities on the other side. Each parity therefore costs at least two cover-member incidences. The two integral side polygons give closed minors attaining all eight incidences.
